g.text: Serving Stack - PagedAttention vs FlashAttention vs the whole SOTA picture
Explained on: Beyond → Serving stack & scheduler · sessions 08 FlashAttention, 10 PagedAttention | vLLM 2309.06180 | FlashAttention 2205.14135 | FlashAttention-2 2307.08691
1 Two different questions: WHERE is KV stored? vs HOW is attention computed?
Where do I store KV, and how is it allocated, grown, shared and freed?
Memory management: the cache manager / block allocator
Fixed 16-token blocks + a block table (OS virtual memory for KV)
External fragmentation, growth without copying, sharing; waste < 16 tokens/seq
20.4-38.2% KV utilization before -> waste < 4%; 2-4x throughput vs FT / Orca
shrink KV: M_KV = 2 * L * B * T * H_kv * d_h * S is unchanged
Efficient Memory Management for LLM Serving with PagedAttention, arXiv 2309.06180
How do I compute attention while minimizing HBM <-> SRAM traffic?
Tile Q, K, V into on-chip SRAM + online softmax; never write T x T to HBM
HBM reads/writes of the score matrix; extra score memory O(T^2) -> O(T)
Exact (not approximate) output; FA-2: better parallelism and work partitioning
shrink KV, allocate KV, or decide which requests run
A 10 GB KV cache stays 10 GB under FlashAttention - it just reads the pieces efficiently.
PagedAttention likewise does not shrink it: it only stops you wasting the memory around it.
2 The T x T problem and the tiling picture (FlashAttention)
S = Q K^T / sqrt(d_h) S in R^(T x T)
FP16: 10^10 x 2 B = 20 GB per head, per layer
Standard: write S to HBM, read it back for softmax,
write P, read it again for P V
FlashAttention: S never exists in HBM
Writes S (T x T) to HBM
HBM (slow, big: 40 GB, 1.555 TB/s on A100 40 GB)
K (T x d_h, per KV head)
V (T x d_h, per KV head)
SRAM / registers (fast, tiny: hundreds of KiB per SM) - the inner loop lives here
Example B_r = B_c = 64, d_h = 128: Q_i, K_j, V_j = 16 KiB each (FP16), S_ij = 16 KiB (FP32), O_i = 32 KiB (FP32)
=> ~96 KiB on-chip. HBM traffic: Q and O touched once, K and V streamed once per Q tile, no T x T write.
Online softmax for one Q tile i (rows = B_r)
for j = 1 .. T / B_c: # stream K_j, V_j
S = Q_i K_j^T / sqrt(d_h) (B_r x B_c)
m' = max( m , rowmax(S) ) new running max
P = exp( S - m' ) (B_r x B_c)
a = exp( m - m' ) rescale factor
l = a * l + rowsum(P) running denominator
O = a * O + P V_j (B_r x d_h)
O_i = O / l write O_i to HBM once
Why rescale? When a larger max appears, everything accumulated so far was
computed against the OLD max. Multiplying l and O by a = exp(m - m') re-bases
it to the new max. The final O_i = softmax(S) V is EXACT - not an approximation.
Only m, l (B_r numbers) are carried between tiles - never the T x T matrix.
Worked row: tile 1 scores [1, 3] -> m = 3, l = e^-2 + 1 = 1.1353
3 Combined pipeline: PagedAttention says WHERE, the kernel says HOW
PagedAttention territory: KV blocks are HERE
PagedAttention tells the system: KV blocks are here. The kernel says: I will process those blocks efficiently.
In a paged kernel each 16-token KV block can serve as one K/V tile: the block table is the tile iterator
(tile j -> physical block table[j]), and the online-softmax update from section 2 runs unchanged.
4 Five different problems, and the long-context menu
Can GPU read KV fast enough?
1,000,000-token context, sharded along the sequence axis
ring: each GPU passes its K,V block to its neighbour while computing on the one it holds (overlap comm with compute)
KV per GPU = total / 4 (toy GQA-8: 65.5 GB total -> ~16.4 GB each)
Attention stays EXACT: every Q must still see every earlier K,V (causal)
Bottleneck MOVES: HBM capacity -> NVLink / InfiniBand bandwidth.
Prefill (ring attention): every layer ships K,V shards around the ring, overlapped with compute.
Decode: each GPU attends its local shard; only partial (O, m, l) are merged (online-softmax merge)
- a few KB per layer per step.
how much historical information must exist
GQA | MQA | MLA | CLA | SSM | Hybrid
Paged KV | prefix cache | KV quant | offload | eviction | block allocator
continuous batching | chunked prefill | speculative decoding | memory-aware sched. | P/D disagg.
VRAM capacity | HBM bandwidth | tensor cores | NVLink
Order matters: does it FIT (steps 1-3) -> is memory WASTED (4) -> is each piece FAST (5-6) -> who RUNS (7)
-> extreme context (8) -> user-visible latency: TTFT (9) and TPOT (10). Colors = layer that owns the fix (see section 7).
shrinks KV or removes the bytes decode must
read per token - that is the model's job
GQA/MLA/SSM decide how much historical information must exist; PagedAttention decides how that information is allocated and reclaimed;
FlashAttention decides how efficiently attention consumes it; and the scheduler decides which requests are allowed to occupy the GPU at each iteration.
